name: PayPal Holdings

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Runs a two-sided digital wallet network (PayPal, Venmo) plus unbranded card processing (Braintree). It earns fees on payment volume: $1.79T of volume in 2025, $487B in 3Q'26.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Transaction revenues $7.71B of $8.58B net revenue (90%) in 3Q'26; other value-added services (interest on balances, credit, partners) $873M (10%). Venmo revenue about $1.7B in 2025, up about 20%.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Consumers (440M active accounts, +0.6% y/y) and merchants of all sizes. No top-customer share is disclosed; large merchants get co-marketing incentives booked against revenue.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: 42% of 3Q'26 net revenue from customers outside the US (44% a year earlier); 35% of volume outside the US. Dollar up 4.8% in 3 months is a translation headwind ahead; 3Q'26 was 2% reported vs 1% currency-neutral.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Fee on volume, so recurring in nature. But take rate is slipping: transaction margin dollars $3,950M on $487.1B volume = 0.81%, vs 0.85% a year earlier ($3,871M on $458.1B), as mix shifts to low-margin Braintree.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Transaction expense is 49.5% of revenue ($4,248M of $8,584M) and grew 4.6% against revenue +2%. Capex $852M in 2025 (2.6% of revenue), so asset-light. Restructuring $255M in 3Q'26. Guidance: raised FY26 non-GAAP EPS to about $5.60 (from about $5.38 in July) but Feb 2026 admitted execution gaps.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: Visa/Mastercard network and bank fees (processors may pass fee increases on to PayPal, 10-K risk factor), bank funding rails, data centres (migrating to cloud through 2028), BNPL funding via loan sales ($18.2B sold). Single points: the two networks; FCA is probing PayPal's Visa/Mastercard contract terms. Pass-through is partial: transaction expense rose faster than revenue and merchant incentives are netted from revenue. Signal tags: rates (lower rates cut interest on balances; OVAS -2% in 3Q), dollar (42% non-US revenue), hy_spreads (BNPL funding), regulation (interchange/network fees).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Network of 440M accounts and 6.8B transactions in the quarter; Venmo is a distinct US habit. Doing differently now: selling BNPL receivables, a bank partner revenue share (+$90M 9M), PYUSD stablecoin. But the edge in branded checkout is contested (see read 10).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Would be noticed if gone: 60.8 payments per active account per year (+6%), 6.8B transactions in 3Q'26 (+7%). Sales and marketing $508M = 5.9% of revenue, modest for a consumer brand.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Management said execution 'has not been where it needs to be, particularly in branded checkout' (Feb 2026), and by Q2 said branded checkout 'further stabilized'. Revenue from PayPal-branded products fell about $240M in 3Q'26 while Braintree rose about $270M. No quantified branded-checkout growth figure is in the filings reached.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Venmo revenue +$100M y/y in 3Q'26, loan portfolio income rising, Braintree volume up. Total volume +6% in 3Q'26 but transaction margin dollars only +2%, so growth is not yet converting.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: 2025 operating cash flow $6.4B, FCF $5.6B (adjusted $6.4B); 3Q'26 FCF $1.4B. Cash and investments $15.1B vs debt $13.5B. Buybacks $6.0B over 12 months (117M shares); share count 1,171M (Jan 2021) to 831M (Oct 2026). 2026 buyback prices about $45-54 per share, below 2021-24 levels. Pay rewards transaction margin dollars and non-GAAP operating income (annual) and relative TSR vs S&P 500 (3-year). New CEO from HP (March 2026); CFO leaves Feb 2027. Insider ownership table not extracted.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: ZOOM TEST: not failed, not passed. Against 'losing relevance': 440M accounts, transactions +7%, transactions per account +6%, volume +9% for nine months, volume 2025 $1.79T. For it: active accounts +0.6% over a year (438M to 440M), management concedes branded checkout execution problems, PayPal-branded revenue is falling on mix and merchant incentives, and GAAP operating income fell 8% in 3Q'26. Verdict: a large, still-used network whose monetisation of its own brand is eroding, not a vanishing product. Key-person risk: CEO and CFO both new within 12 months.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Clean: no Item 4.01/4.02 8-Ks, no NT filings, no material weakness found in 3 years scanned. Cautions: three SEC comment letters in May-Aug 2025 on revenue disaggregation (closed with company replies); securities class actions (Darcy, filed Feb 2026, alleges concealed branded-checkout problems; Norfolk, Apr 2026); CFPB CIDs; FY26 non-GAAP adjustments about $570M; critical audit matter on consumer loan allowance.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +: e-commerce volume. Overheat 0: nominal volume up, interest on balances helps, strong dollar hurts 42% non-US revenue. Stagflation -: discretionary volume and take rate squeezed. Slowdown -: volume slows, consumer credit losses (transaction and credit losses $386M in 3Q) rise, though lower rates only trim float income.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Open: CFPB civil investigative demands on Reg E and PayPal Credit; UK FCA Competition Act investigation into PayPal's Visa/Mastercard terms (notice March 2026); several shareholder suits; Hawaii consumer-protection suit.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $57.81, EV about $46.4B (market cap $48.0B less $1.6B net cash). EV/EBITDA 6.6x on 2025 EBITDA $7.0B; P/E about 10.3x on FY26 non-GAAP guide ($5.60), 11.4x GAAP ($5.07). Own year-end GAAP P/E: 53x (2021), 34x, 16x, 21x, 11x (2025). Peers trailing GAAP P/E: MA 40x, GPN 17x, FISV 9x. Reverse DCF at 10%/3%: price implies owner FCF (FCF less stock pay, $4.6B) shrinking 2.2% a year for 10 years (5.0% a year on reported FCF $5.6B); own 2020-25 FCF growth was +0.8% a year. Cushion is real; it assumes decline.

status_reason: Quality B and a real price cushion (about 12% FCF yield), but branded-checkout share trend is unquantified and the 2% transaction-margin growth does not yet show the turn; evidence incomplete.
the_mistake: Candidate, not yet proven: the market prices PayPal as a shrinking franchise (owner FCF down about 2% a year for a decade) while volume, transactions per account, Venmo and Braintree are growing and FCF funds a 29% share count cut in under 6 years. It treats Braintree-driven margin dilution as permanent loss of the branded wallet.
what_makes_market_notice: Q4'26 results and 2027 outlook (early Feb 2027, date not confirmed) showing branded-checkout stabilisation in numbers; new CFO starts Feb 3, 2027. Transaction margin dollars growth moving above volume growth would be the proof.

feedback.fact: Card-volume data have not turned: PayPal volume +6% (+7% currency-neutral) and transactions +7% in 3Q'26
feedback.effect: confirms Overheat hard data; real-spending softness not visible in payments volume yet

feedback.fact: Interest on customer balances fell on lower rates (other value-added services revenue -2% y/y in 3Q'26)
feedback.effect: rates effect on float income; a Fed hike would help this line

feedback.fact: Revenue +2% reported vs +1% currency-neutral in 3Q'26; 42% of revenue non-US
feedback.effect: answers lead L-20261126-markets-7: dollar was a small tailwind in 3Q; the 3-month dollar rise is a headwind to come

coverage_notes.presentation: Earnings decks are not attached to the 8-K on EDGAR; IR site page reached was a navigation shell with no figures. Branded checkout growth is therefore not quantified.
coverage_notes.10-Q: 3Q'26 10-Q read in text; 1Q and 2Q 10-Qs via 8-K earnings releases and XBRL facts only.
coverage_notes.def14a: Pay design read; beneficial-ownership table for officers and directors as a group not extracted.
coverage_notes.red_flag_scan: Filing list 2022-02 to 2026-11-24 scanned for Items 4.01/4.02, NT forms, CORRESP/UPLOAD; two 2025 CORRESP letters read, UPLOAD PDFs not opened.
